Patch Set 4:

(5 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good functionally; a few optional notes inline about the accuracy of the new warnings and documentation. No need to re-spin for them alone. The new probing has no test coverage. If mdadm is available on the test nodes, would a conf-sanity case that builds a small raid5 over loop devices and checks the resulting stride/stripe_width (dumpe2fs -h) be feasible?

* Verified+1 (copy condition: "changekind:NO_CHANGE OR changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE")

Patch Set 5:

Patch Set 5: rebased onto current master. The only conflict was the .TH date line in mkfs.lustre.8.

It also has the fixes for the Patch Set 4 AI review comments:
- The power-of-two row warning is now for parity arrays only. raid0 and raid10 do not get it.
- The mount check now compares the stripe that mballoc really uses: -o stripe=, then stripe_width, then stride.
- A partition of an md array (for example an LVM PV on md0p1) is now probed.
- Wording fixes in the comments and in mkfs.lustre.8. mount.lustre.8 now has an entry for stripe=.

Compile-tested only. Not tested on a real md array after these changes.

commit.subject: LU-20564 utils: probe md RAID geometry for OST mkfs/mount
commit.message:
LU-20564 utils: probe md RAID geometry for OST mkfs/mount

mkfs.lustre now probes the md array under an OST target, through any
stacked dm devices, and seeds -E stride/stripe_width so mballoc can
align allocations to full stripes.  mke2fs can derive these from the
blkid topology, but dm-cache replaces optimal_io_size with its block
size when that does not divide the row.  LVM thin and VDO pools are
not probed through, as they remap each block.  An md array whose
members report their own optimal_io_size (raid0 over raid6, or over
hardware RAID LUNs) that does not divide the chunk is left to mke2fs
and the blkid topology, as is any volume that spans one.  raid0,
raid4/5/6, raid10 and raidkm (level 71) are decoded, and user-supplied
values are respected.  mount.lustre warns when an OST on a parity
array has no fs geometry, or geometry that is not a multiple of the
array row, unless it is mounted with -o stripe=.  l_tunedisk skips
this check.

mkfs.lustre also warns about two things that cannot be corrected once
the OST is formatted: a partition that does not start on a stripe
boundary, and, on parity arrays, a data row (k * chunk) that is not a
power of two.  The default bulk RPC sizes are powers of two, so a row
that is not one leaves a partial row at the tail of every RPC, which
the array services as a read-modify-write.  It also warns when the row
is larger than the default 4MiB RPC, which can be fixed later by
raising brw_size on the OSS, up to its 64MiB limit.  A larger row is
reported as unfixable.  mkfs.lustre.8 gains a RAID ALIGNMENT section
covering these, and how to correct them.

Tested on RHEL 9.7 against live loop-backed md arrays: raid0/4/5/6,
raid10 near/far/offset, a non-power-of-two row, user-supplied values,
dm-linear over one array and spanning two, an LVM PV on an md
partition, dm-cache, and misaligned partition starts.  Also tested
against live raidkm arrays, plain and declustered.  In every case the
computed row matches md's own queue/optimal_io_size.  LVM thin and
VDO volumes on md get no geometry and no warning, and the mount
check was run against matching and mismatched geometry.
